reasons: The sliding gate is a 1.5m black wrought iron gate with vertical uprights, set in the existing 4200mm driveway opening behind a retained low brick wall and a 3m verge. Its open-work form keeps the bungalow and frontage visible, and the wall, verge, planting and mature trees are retained. It is therefore considered to respect the host property and street scene, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 41 and 44 and NPPF paragraphs 135 and 140. Pier details and the finish are to be secured by condition.

The gate sits behind a 3m grass verge and slides behind the existing wall, so it does not swing over the verge or footpath. Existing parking is unchanged and the Highway Authority supports the proposal without conditions, as no pedestrian visibility splay is needed. No unacceptable highway safety impact would arise, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policy 13 and NPPF paragraphs 115 and 116.

The gate is located on the street frontage, away from the side boundaries shared with Nos. 44 and 48, and has an open-work form. It would not cause overbearing, overshadowing or loss of privacy, and no neighbour amenity concern is recorded. The proposal is therefore considered acceptable and in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 10 and 44 and NPPF paragraph 135.

The site lies in Flood Zones 2 and 3, but the proposal is minor householder development within the curtilage of an existing dwelling. It creates no floorspace or impermeable area and its vertical bars would not impede flood flows. Neither the sequential test nor the exception test is required, and no flood or drainage conflict arises, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 56 and 57 and NPPF paragraphs 176 and 181.

The existing brick wall, verge, footpath, planting and trees are retained and the gate fits within the existing opening, so harm to trees and habitats is unlikely. A condition will protect frontage trees and planting, and their roots, during installation of posts and tracks. The proposal is therefore considered acceptable and in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 30 and 32 and NPPF paragraphs 136 and 187.

The proposal is a householder alteration to an existing dwelling in Skellow, with no change of use and no new dwelling. It is acceptable in principle within a settlement, subject to the design, amenity, highway and flood matters assessed above, and the flood risk sequential test is not engaged. It is therefore in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 1, 10 and 57.

The gate would not generate noise, air or other pollution beyond ordinary domestic use. No contamination or land stability constraint is recorded, and no new sensitive occupiers are introduced, so a preliminary risk assessment is not warranted. Statutory undertakers raise no objection. The proposal is therefore considered acceptable and in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 54 and 55 and NPPF paragraphs 187, 196 and 198.
conditions: The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission. Reason: Required by Section 91 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the approved plans and documents listed on the decision notice. Reason: To ensure that the development is carried out in accordance with the application as approved.

Before the gate is installed, details of the gate piers (including dimensions, brick type and cap material) and the gate finish shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The gate and piers shall be constructed in accordance with the approved details and the gate shall be finished in black. Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance that respects the character of the host property and street scene, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policies 41 and 44.

No existing trees, hedges or shrubs on or adjoining the site frontage shall be removed, lopped or topped as part of the development, and any excavation for gate posts, sliding track or foundations shall be hand-dug and avoid severing roots over 25mm diameter. Any tree or hedge removed or damaged in breach of this shall be replaced in the next planting season with a native species of a size and species agreed in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Reason: To protect trees and planting that contribute to public amenity and ecological interest, in accordance with Doncaster Local Plan Policy 32.
